params.body:
Phase 1, step 3 of `docs/design/sources-before-more-sources.md`.

The outcome of a run went to a log file and nowhere else, so "silent since when"
could be asked of nothing. TikTok's actor stopped returning anything on 12 May;
finding that date in September meant reading the signals table backwards,
because no row anywhere said "this adapter ran and got nothing".

## `adapter_runs`

One row per adapter per collect round: outcome, `fetched` and `fresh` kept apart
(NULL when the adapter does not say, since a zero would read as a measurement),
the reason, the duration and the declared cost. Cost is charged only when the
adapter actually tried: a skipped run called nobody.

Every way out of the collector's loop now goes through one `finish()`, so the
run that delivered, the one that crashed and the one that never got its turn are
all on record. Writing it down may never cost the round itself: a full disk
loses a row, not the signals.

## `adapterStanding()`

Last run, last delivery, and the streak of non-deliveries with the date it
began. The test that matters pins 12 May as `silentSince` for a TikTok history
replayed from the real one.

A streak is broken by `nothing-new` as well as by `delivered`. An upstream that
answers with items we already know is alive; calling that silence would make a
weekly source read as broken six days out of seven.

`recordsSince` travels along, so "never delivered" reads as "not since" and not
as a fact about all time. Rows are kept 120 days.

No judgement here. The adapter declares what it expects, Elixir judges.

750 tests pass, 8 new. Next: the Apify helper.
params.title: Every adapter run is written down
